gemini.rationale: The transaction was a whole-company acquisition where USG Corporation was acquired by Knauf. The product/asset tier (T4) and operational processes (T5) transferred together as a complete business, so there is no gap_45. The organization (T6) also transferred with the business, despite the replacement of the top executive team and board, so there is no structural gap_56.

grok.rationale: The deal was a whole-company cash merger in which Merger Sub merged into USG and USG survived as an indirect wholly-owned Knauf subsidiary, so the customer-facing product lines (Gypsum, Ceilings, Performance Materials, USG Boral, etc.) and the operating processes that produce them crossed the ownership boundary together inside the same surviving legal entity; gap_45 is therefore 0. At closing the entire pre-deal board and named executive officers ceased and a Knauf-appointed slate was installed, but Continuing USG Employees were contractually carried under a fixed-term compensation/benefits continuity covenant through the following December 31, so the operational workforce that runs T5 processes transferred alongside those processes and gap_56 is 0.

openai.rationale: The whole-company merger left USG as the surviving corporation and transferred it, including its building-products businesses, into Knauf ownership; the slice documents no separation of those products from their associated operating processes, so gap_45 is 0. At closing, however, all incumbent directors and named executive officers ceased their roles and were replaced by a small new slate, while the broader workforce received only a fixed-term compensation-and-benefits continuity covenant, documenting a process-versus-organization mismatch for gap_56. No transitional-services or operating agreement allocating that mismatch is documented.
